chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about the trustee: 'Would he pay the Zakat al-Fitr on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth?' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'There is no Zakat upon an orphan.'

key_terms.زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the alms-tax of breaking the fast)
key_terms.لَا زَكَاةَ عَلَى يَتِيمٍ: There is no Zakat upon an orphan

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat al-Fitr obligatory on orphans who have wealth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a concise ruling that orphans are exempt from Zakat al-Fitr, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the obligation is tied to the individual's capacity and status rather than mere wealth possession. This hadith highlights the benevolent legal nuance in Shia fiqh, where the trustee pays on behalf of the orphan if necessary, but the primary exemption underscores the protection of the vulnerable's assets. The ruling is rooted in the principle that Zakat al-Fitr is a purification for the payer, and for an orphan whose wealth is managed by a guardian, the direct obligation is lifted to preserve their resources.
